title: Minimum Number of Pushes to Type Word II
summary: Given a string of lowercase English letters, determine the minimum number of key presses required to type the string after remapping keys 2 through 9 to distinct collections of letters.
statement: Given a string of lowercase English letters, determine the minimum number of key presses required to type the string after remapping keys 2 through 9 to distinct collections of letters. Each letter must be mapped to exactly one key, and the keypads have predefined mappings for letters a, b, and c on key 2. The goal is to find the optimal remapping to minimize the total key presses.
constraints: word is a nonempty lowercase string.
Eight keys are available; the first assigned letter on a key costs one push, the second two, and so on.
Remap all letters to minimize the total pushes needed to type word.
hints: The keypad offers eight slots at each push depth, and frequent letters should take cheaper slots.
Sort letter frequencies descending and assign them to costs 1 repeated eight times, then 2 repeated eight times, and so on.
For sorted frequency at index i, add frequency*(i//8+1).
An exchange placing a higher frequency in a cheaper slot never increases cost, so descending frequencies paired with ascending slot costs is optimal.
editorial: An exchange placing a higher frequency in a cheaper slot never increases cost, so descending frequencies paired with ascending slot costs is optimal.

tests.explanation: Five distinct letters fit in one-push slots, so the five-character word costs five.
The three letters each occupy a one-push slot and occur four times, totaling twelve.
